Let me approach this from a chemistry perspective. When acids react with salts, typically an acid-base reaction occurs. In this case, carboxylic acids (weak acids) would react with cyanide salts (which contain the CN- anion, a relatively strong base).

The general reaction would be:
RCOOH + CN- → RCOO- + HCN

The carboxylic acid donates a proton to the cyanide ion, forming the carboxylate anion and hydrogen cyanide (HCN), which is a gas at room temperature.

Based on my chemistry knowledge and the reaction mechanism, when carboxylic acids react with cyanide salts, hydrogen cyanide gas (HCN) is produced. This corresponds to option C.
